description: Run one structured program/argv command. Manual and auto-approved modes use Runtime policy plus the Anthropic workspace sandbox. User-confirmed dangerous mode runs directly as the current OS user with host filesystem, working-directory, environment, and internet access and no EASY CODE approval prompt. Explicit one-shot shells remain supported.

propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name or workspace-relative executable; absolute host executables require dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.args: The structured argument vector passed directly to the program. Never repeat program in args[0]. For cmd /c, the entire shell command must be ONE argument: program=cmd, args=["/c","dir /b"], cwd=".". For simple directory listing prefer search_files mode=list, without a shell.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Workspace-relative existing directory, or an absolute host directory only in dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.intent: The purpose of the command, used by Runtime when applying execution policy. Use verify for a validation command that is not accurately described by the legacy test or build intents.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Required when intent is verify and forbidden for inspect, run, or install. It may optionally classify legacy test/build calls as unit_test, integration_test, build, typecheck, lint, format_check, smoke_test, benchmark, or custom.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested command-phase timeout. Runtime applies the minimum of this request, the configured command limit, and the classified capability limit, then returns all four timeout values including the effective limit.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Prefer existing project scripts and one synchronous command for short checks. Put the executable only in program. Classify verification accurately using the schema. One-shot shells are allowed; interactive, login, encoded or detached shells and shell-level backgrounding are forbidden. Use start_command for supervised background work. Never bypass Runtime policy, approval or sandbox failures; retry only when Runtime explicitly permits a bounded recovery. Treat a turn-scoped sandbox pause as a pause, not a permanent code/DAG failure.
